title: 第三章 一碗冷饭第四章 不肯跪
content_zh:
井在村子东头。
江砚挑着空桶，走得很慢。倒不全是因为身子虚——是这一路上的光景，让他越走，心里越沉。
整个沈家村，统共二三十户人家，可这一路走来，没几间屋子是齐整的。墙塌了的，门没了的，屋顶上的茅草被风掀走大半、露出黑黢黢的椽子的，到处都是。有几家门口贴着早褪了色的旧符，门板却虚掩着，里头黑洞洞地没声响——江砚猜，那些人家，要么逃了，要么，没了。
路上偶尔遇见个人，也都是面黄肌瘦，缩着脖子匆匆赶路，眼神躲闪。没人跟他打招呼，倒有个抱着柴的老汉，离老远就往旁边让，像是怕沾上什么晦气。
江砚心里那点关于“古代”的、从影视剧里来的模糊想象，被这真实的破败，碾得粉碎。
什么田园牧歌，什么古风雅韵。这里只有冷、饿、和一种弥漫在空气里的、人人自危的死气。
他在井边遇见了今天第一桩“事”。
井台边已经有人在打水了，是个十六七岁的半大小子，膀大腰圆，穿一件还算厚实的旧棉袄——在这村里，算是“富态”的了。江砚的记忆告诉他：这是大伯的小儿子，他名义上的堂兄，江狗剩。
也是这十几年来，揍他揍得最勤快的人。
江狗剩一眼瞧见他，咧开嘴，露出一口黄牙：“哟，废物起来了？”
江砚没理他，自顾自把桶往井里放。
“跟你说话呢，装聋？”江狗剩一脚踹翻了江砚刚提上来、晃晃悠悠的半桶水，水泼了一地，瞬间在雪上结起一层薄冰。他叉着腰，居高临下，“爹说今儿二叔家来收账，家里要紧着用人。你那份口粮，省下来招待客人了。听见没？”
江砚动作顿了一下。
省他的口粮。也就是说，他今天，连那碗掺糠的冷饭，都没有了。
搁原主身上，这会儿八成已经缩着脖子、点头哈腰地应了。可江砚不是原主。他直起身，平静地看着江狗剩：“不给我饭，活我也不干。”
这话一出，江狗剩明显愣了一下。
这怂货，今天吃错药了？
“你说啥？”江狗剩往前逼了一步，伸手就来揪江砚的衣领，“你他娘的再说一遍——”
江砚这回学乖了。他没硬挺着挨揍，在江狗剩的手够到他之前，侧身让开了半步。这一让，让得不算利索，到底是身子跟不上脑子，可总归是没让对方一把揪住。
江狗剩扑了个空，恼羞成怒，反手一拳就砸了过来。

这一拳，江砚没能躲开。拳头结结实实砸在他肩膀上，把他打得倒退两步，撞在井台的石沿上，疼得他眼前金星直冒。
“跑啊，你倒是接着跑啊！”江狗剩得了势，又是一脚。
江砚护着头蹲了下去。
他不是不想还手。是真的还不了。这具身子的力气，连个十二三岁的孩子都未必打得过，更别说眼前这膀大腰圆的。硬碰硬，他只会被打得更惨。
他抱着头，挨了两脚，把那口要骂出去的脏话，硬生生咽了回去。
心里却记下了。
江狗剩。还有他背后这一家子。这笔账，先记着。
“起来！”江狗剩踹够了，喘着粗气，“水挑回去！客人快到了，误了事，看我爹不打断你的腿！”说完，他拎起自己那两桶满满的水，晃晃悠悠地走了，临走还回头啐了一口。
江砚在雪地里蹲了好一会儿。
肩膀火烧火燎地疼，肚子里空空荡荡，发出一阵细微的绞动。这具身子，大概昨天那顿饭也没吃饱。
content_en:
The well is at the east end of the village.
Jiang Yan walked slowly while carrying the empty bucket. It wasn't all because of his physical weakness - it was the scenery along the way that made his heart sink more and more as he walked.
There are a total of twenty or thirty households in Shenjia Village, but along the way, few houses are neat. Walls collapsed, doors were missing, and most of the thatch on the roof was blown away by the wind, exposing the black rafters, everywhere. There were some houses with long-faded old charms pasted on their doors, but the door panels were ajar, and it was dark and silent inside—Jiang Yan guessed that those families had either escaped or disappeared.
Occasionally I meet people on the road, and they all have sallow faces and thin muscles, hurriedly walking with their necks hunched, and their eyes evasive. No one greeted him, but there was an old man holding firewood who stepped aside as if he was far away, as if he was afraid of getting into any bad luck.
Jiang Yan's vague imagination about "ancient times" that came from movies and TV shows was crushed to pieces by this real dilapidation.
What pastoral songs, what ancient elegance. There is only cold, hunger, and a sense of death that permeates the air and makes everyone feel in danger.
He met the first "thing" of the day at the well.
Someone was already fetching water at the well. He was a young boy of sixteen or seventeen years old, with broad shoulders and a round waist. He wore a relatively thick old cotton-padded jacket - he was considered "rich" in this village. Jiang Yan's memory told him: This is his uncle's youngest son, his nominal cousin, Jiang Goucheng.
He was also the person who beat him the most diligently in the past ten years.
Jiang Gou Sheng saw him at a glance and grinned, showing his yellow teeth: "Hey, are you useless?"
Jiang Yan ignored him and put the bucket into the well.
"I'm talking to you, are you pretending to be deaf?" Jiang Goucheng kicked over the half-bucket of water that Jiang Yan had just brought up and was dangling. The water splashed all over the ground, instantly forming a thin layer of ice on the snow. He put his hands on his hips and said condescendingly, "Dad said that my second uncle's family is coming to collect the bill today, and the family is very busy with employees. Your share of rations can be saved to entertain guests. Do you hear me?"
Jiang Yan paused.
Save his rations. In other words, he didn't even have that bowl of cold rice mixed with chaff today.
If you put it on the original owner, most likely he would have shrunk his neck, nodded and bowed in response. But Jiang Yan is not the original owner. He straightened up and looked at Jiang Goucheng calmly: "If you don't give me food, I won't do any work."
As soon as these words came out, Jiang Goucheng was obviously stunned.
This coward, did you take the wrong medicine today?
"What did you say?" Jiang Gouchen took a step forward and reached out to grab Jiang Yan's collar, "You fucking say it again-"
Jiang Yan learned well this time. He didn't stand up to be beaten. Before Jiang Goucheng's hand could reach him, he stepped aside half a step. This concession was not very neat. After all, the body could not keep up with the brain, but it was still not caught by the other party.
Jiang Goucheng missed him, became angry, and punched him with his backhand.
Jiang Yan couldn't dodge this punch. The fist hit him firmly on the shoulder, knocking him back two steps and hitting the stone edge of the well platform. The pain was so painful that stars popped out of his eyes.
"Run, you should keep running!" Jiang Goucheng got the upper hand and kicked him again.
Jiang Yan squatted down, protecting his head.
It's not that he doesn't want to fight back. I really can’t pay it back. The strength of this body may not even be able to beat a twelve or thirteen-year-old child, let alone the one in front of him who is so big and round. If he goes head-on, he will only get beaten worse.
He held his head, was kicked twice, and swallowed back the curse words he wanted to say.
But he remembered it in his heart.
Jiang Gouzheng. And the family behind him. Remember this account first.
"Get up!" Jiang Goucheng gasped after kicking enough, "Take the water back! The guests are coming soon. If you miss something, let's see if my father doesn't break your legs!" After saying that, he picked up his two full buckets of water and walked away unsteadily. Before leaving, he turned back and spat.
Jiang Yan squatted in the snow for a long time.
My shoulders were burning with pain, my stomach was empty, and I let out a small groan.Wringing. This body probably wasn't even full from yesterday's meal.
